title: PostgreSQL 18 Documentation: Reliability and the Write-Ahead Log
why: Primary account of PostgreSQL's WAL, checkpointing and crash recovery, to contrast with SQLite's rollback-journal and WAL designs.

title: PostgreSQL 18 Documentation: Concurrency Control
why: Official chapter on MVCC and snapshot visibility whose sub-pages give the READ COMMITTED/REPEATABLE READ/SERIALIZABLE guarantees, explicit row locks and deadlock handling.

title: PostgreSQL 18 Documentation: Routine Vacuuming
why: Definitive description of dead tuples, old-version retention, long transactions, transaction ID wraparound and autovacuum for the MVCC cleanup chapter.

title: Atomic Commit In SQLite
why: SQLite's own account of its rollback-journal commit protocol, sector-write and ordering assumptions, and hot-journal recovery.

title: SQLite Write-Ahead Logging
why: How SQLite's WAL mode actually works: checkpoints, snapshots, reader/writer interaction, and the WAL-reset corruption bug and its fix.

title: Isolation In SQLite
why: Short authoritative statement of SQLite's actual isolation behaviour and read transactions in rollback-journal and WAL modes.

title: ARIES: A Transaction Recovery Method Supporting Fine-Granularity Locking and Partial Rollbacks Using Write-Ahead Logging
version: ACM Transactions on Database Systems 17(1), March 1992, pp. 94-162
why: The original ARIES paper: redo/undo logging, LSNs, the analysis/redo/undo restart phases, and fuzzy checkpoints.

title: Serializable Snapshot Isolation in PostgreSQL
why: Design and implementation of PostgreSQL's SERIALIZABLE level, covering write-skew detection, dangerous structures and serialization failures.
